known_omissions: FATF Recommendations 10 and 11 and the FinCEN customer due diligence rule at 31 CFR 1010.230 could not be retrieved live because the publishers blocked automated access, so the beneficial ownership threshold, the control prong and the five-year record-keeping rule are represented only through HMRC and EU proxies and are marked as unverified detail.

The ISO 20022 e-Repository page for the CashAccount business component and the ISO 13616 IBAN Registry file did not render for this research, so element-level ISO 20022 and IBAN detail is grounded in the Bundesbank and Open Banking renderings and treated as alignment rather than verified normative text.

United States state unclaimed-property dormancy periods and the Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act could not be verified, so only the United Kingdom fifteen-year statutory test is cited and dormancy is treated as jurisdictional.
Securities and custody account internal structure, including position holdings, safekeeping accounts and segregation of client assets, is only classified, not decomposed.
Islamic and profit-sharing account structures, notional pooling, virtual account hierarchies and escrow or client-money segregation rules are under-modelled and no primary source was secured.
Tokenised deposit and account-based digital currency identifier schemes are acknowledged only through the CRS depository-account expansion and are otherwise not modelled.
Payment card account specifics beyond a masked primary account number as an identifier scheme are not modelled.
conflicts: Deposit protection algebra differs by regime: the United States applies a per-depositor, per-insured-bank, per-ownership-category limit of USD 250 000, while the European Union applies EUR 100 000 per depositor per credit institution with per-depositor treatment of joint accounts. A single insured indicator is therefore unsafe and the model carries scheme-scoped designations only.

The United States account-data-sharing obligation is unsettled: the Personal Financial Data Rights rule was issued in October 2024, but the Bureau opened a reconsideration by advance notice in August 2025. Conformance must not be asserted, and the access designation records the obligation status as contested.

Denomination cardinality conflicts across projections: the Open Banking v4.0 resource makes currency mandatory except for switched accounts, while ontology and message-standard views permit multi-denomination and non-currency-denominated ledger accounts. The model keeps denomination as a zero-to-many reference and records the conflict per projection.

Tax classification is time-versioned: the depository account definition expands on 1 January 2026 to specified electronic money products and central bank digital currencies, so a classification field without an effective period would misstate history.

No normative global account status code list was found. Interface enumerations such as enabled and disabled do not align with core-banking states such as dormant, blocked and escheated, so status is carried as a scheme-qualified code rather than as a canonical enumeration.

Dormancy thresholds conflict across jurisdictions, with a fifteen-year statutory test in the United Kingdom against materially shorter periods elsewhere, so dormancy cannot be expressed as a global constant.
regional_assumptions: IBAN-first identification is assumed only for the European Economic Area and other adopting countries; United States accounts are identified by routing number plus account number and many jurisdictions use a domestic basic bank account number alone.

The payment account, basic-features account, fee information document, statement of fees and switching-service constructs are assumed only for European Union and European Economic Area consumer payment accounts.

Deposit guarantee constructs follow the European Union directive for European accounts and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation framework for United States insured depository institutions; other jurisdictions operate different schemes not modelled here.
HMRC manual pages are used as an accessible rendering of the Common Reporting Standard; implementing legislation and excluded-account lists vary by jurisdiction.
The fifteen-year dormancy test and the reclaim-fund mechanism are United Kingdom specific and are not assumed elsewhere.
The Open Banking Read/Write API v4.0 projection reflects the United Kingdom ecosystem; other open-finance frameworks expose different account resources and permission models.
adversarial_checks: Tested whether balance computation belongs here. Rejected: balances are declared observations with a type, a denomination reference and an as-of instant, and derivation from entries is left to the contained posting model, with mismatches recorded as discrepancies rather than corrected locally.
Tested whether currency, minor units or conversion belong here. Rejected: denomination is a pure outbound reference, and the reference finding carries no unit semantics at all.

Tested whether consent evaluation, enforcement of restrictions or an access audit trail belong here. Rejected: the model carries designations and references, states the requirement that the platform log disclosures, and explicitly disclaims ownership of the audit-trail record model.

Tested whether account and product or contract are separable. Kept separate: the account is the identified container and the terms are a bound instance referencing an external product model, because the same product yields many accounts with divergent bound terms.
Searched for a normative global account status enumeration and for a normative global account type list. None found; recorded as a conflict and a gap rather than inventing a canonical list.

Tested whether opening date plus branch could serve as a natural key. Rejected under the identity priority rule: a date is never an identifier, and both values are carried as attributes with a surrogate identifier minted where no master-system identifier exists.

Tested whether an insured amount should be stored on the account. Rejected: coverage depends on aggregation across a depositor's accounts and is computed by the scheme, so only eligibility and ownership category are designated.

Re-read every bundle, layer, finding and function against the two registered relation rationales. The denomination finding was reduced to a reference-only finding with an inline rationale, and the posting finding was reduced to a container binding that explicitly forbids creating, amending or interpreting postings.

boundaryDecision.rationale: A financial account is an identified, durable container whose identity survives changes to every one of its attributes: holders are added and removed (q-hold-change), classification is re-versioned (q-class-effective), status transitions to terminal states (q-st-transitions) and the identifier itself may or may not survive a switch (q-sw-identifier). Identity independent of attribute values is the entity test, so the account is not a value, not an event and not a reified relationship, even though FIBO models it under client-and-account arrangements. The competing reading, that the true root is the holder-institution arrangement or the relationship or umbrella account above it, is rejected for this model and deferred to a separate account-group model rather than absorbed here, because absorbing it would make the aggregate root variable across jurisdictions and pooling structures. The registry entry_kind value standalone-mm and the research entry_kind value entity are two different vocabularies on two different planes (registry record plane versus subject model plane) and must not be reconciled by overwriting either field; the synthesizer should carry both and stop treating the registry review_state boundary-review-required as unresolved on the entry-kind axis alone. No split or merge is warranted: the account and its bound terms were correctly tested and kept separate, and the CONTAINS edge to WM-ECO-016 keeps posting semantics out.

decisions.concept: Aggregate root: Financial Account as the container root of WM-ECO-015
decisions.rationale: The root is the identified container, not the arrangement and not the ledger. Every finding either identifies the container, binds a party or term to it, records a state of it, or declares a position over it; none of the 26 findings requires a different root to be coherent. The two registered relations resolve the only two places where a rival root could form.

decisions.concept: Account-group, umbrella, relationship and notional-pooling aggregation (declared checklist gap)
decisions.disposition: rejected for this model; deferred to a separate model candidate
decisions.rationale: Pooled and umbrella structures imply an aggregate above the account, which is exactly the pressure that would destabilise this aggregate root. The declared gap admits no primary source was secured. Absorbing it now would widen the root without evidence; registering it as a sibling candidate resolves the gap without scope creep.

decisions.concept: CONTAINS binding to WM-ECO-016 and the posting-container-binding finding
decisions.rationale: The finding carries only a selection key, a read boundary, a partition question and a discrepancy rule, holds no artifact, and its inline_only_rationale explicitly forbids reproducing posting records. This satisfies the ledger matryoshka contract and keeps balance derivation with the contained model.

decisions.concept: The serial account-statement artifact under balance-and-statement-declaration
decisions.disposition: reclassified: retain the statement issuance and delivery designation, move statement content ownership to WM-ECO-016
decisions.rationale: An account statement is a rendering over contained postings, so a serial artifact with media 'statement document' contradicts both the posting-container-binding rationale that forbids holding posting records here and the out_of_scope exclusion of statement rendering. The designation of period, frequency and recipient stays; the rendered instance does not.

The denomination finding carries four questions that are all reference-shaped and an inline_only_rationale that refuses unit codes, minor units and instrument behaviour. No monetary-unit semantics leaked into the pricing, limits or balance findings on inspection.

decisions.concept: Seven neighbour boundary notes with no registered relation row (party master, consent, payment instruction, product catalogue, deposit guarantee scheme, unclaimed property, and the WM-XCT-014 parent)
decisions.disposition: deferred: keep as prose boundary notes in the draft; do not mint typed edges
decisions.rationale: The frozen contract registers only two outbound relations. The boundary notes describe real instance-level references, but publishing them as typed edges without rows in the relations file would create dangling contract state. The parent edge may exist as an inbound row from WM-XCT-014 and must be confirmed, not assumed.

decisions.concept: Coverage checklist statuses for security, privacy, access, retention and interoperability
decisions.rationale: The checklist asserts integrity digests with quarantine on mismatch and a prohibition on shadow copies, but no finding or question carries either. Security has one question, access one, retention one, privacy two. Interoperability claims ISO 20022 component crosswalks that the known omissions admit were never retrieved. The claims exceed their carriers.

decisions.disposition: accepted as reconcilable; wording fix required
decisions.rationale: The 14 documents resolve to 11 distinct publishers once the two EU, two CFPB and two HMRC items are collapsed. The count is defensible but reads as an undercount; the claim must say 14 documents from 11 independent publishers so a reviewer is not left to reconstruct the arithmetic.

decisions.disposition: rejected as stable citations; require immutable pins before publication
decisions.rationale: Both URLs are mutable targets, so the artifact identity rule fails: a reviewer cannot retrieve what was read. FIBO must be pinned to a commit or release tag alongside the stated FBC/20260701 version IRI, and the ISO 20022 catalogue must be pinned by retrieval date and captured message-definition list.

decisions.concept: SRC-013 ISO 13616-1:2020 cited as tier-1 primary support for check-digit validation
decisions.disposition: reclassified to bibliographic reference; evidentiary weight carried by SRC-008
decisions.rationale: The iso.org page is a catalogue entry, and the known omissions confirm the IBAN Registry file did not render. The normative structure text was not read, so validation-and-quality-controls is in substance grounded on the Bundesbank rendering and must say so rather than implying the standard was consulted.

decisions.concept: Beneficial ownership threshold support: q-bo-threshold cited only to SRC-006 (GLEIF LEI) and SRC-010 (HMRC)
decisions.disposition: rejected as adequate support; no threshold or control prong may be asserted
decisions.rationale: GLEIF LEI material identifies legal entities and parent relationships, not AML beneficial ownership determinations, so the cited set contains no authority that states a threshold. The omission note claims EU and HMRC proxies but SRC-004 is not on the finding. The question stays parameterized with the regime named and no numeric value published.

decisions.disposition: deferred: add a second authority or scope the finding regionally before promotion
decisions.rationale: Directive 2014/92/EU addresses fee comparability, switching and basic-features access; it is a thin anchor for q-fee-interest on credit and debit balance interest determination, and it is EU-bound while the finding is stated generally. Single-source, single-jurisdiction support cannot carry a globally phrased finding.

decisions.concept: derive-dormancy-candidacy: three terms (candidacy, designation, determination) for one output, sourced only to SRC-005
decisions.disposition: accepted with rename and jurisdiction parameter
decisions.rationale: The scope statement, the finding and the function each name the same artefact differently, which will fracture downstream references. Normalise to determination, and make the jurisdictional test an explicit input, since the only cited authority is the UK fifteen-year statutory test and the recorded conflict states dormancy cannot be a global constant.

decisions.rationale: q-bo-refresh asks what triggers re-confirmation and q-ev-valid asks what triggers refresh, which implies repeated dated instances rather than one document, and periodic re-provision of depositor information should be confirmed against the guarantee-scheme text. Serial=false on a re-issued instrument breaks artifact identity and supersession.

decisions.concept: assemble-account-context-package sourced to SRC-002 and SRC-009

decisions.rationale: Bootstrap files, bundle structure and resolvable artifact references are Vercy packaging semantics. Neither the Open Banking accounts resource nor the CFPB rule speaks to package assembly, so the citation implies external support that does not exist.

model.name: Financial Transaction / Journal Entry
model.purpose: Model the atomic accounting posting: a balanced set of debit and credit lines recording one economic event in a ledger, with the identity, time, provenance, authority, evidence and retention context an agent needs to create, validate, post, correct, audit and export it.
model.scope_statement: The subject is one journal entry (posting document) treated as an aggregate: an entry header plus two or more posting lines that must balance, together with everything required to establish that the posting is authentic, authorised, correctly timed, correctly measured, and reproducible for audit. It covers the entry as recorded in a ledger of record and as exported for audit or tax inspection. It does not cover the accounts it posts to, the payment or invoice that caused it, or the financial statements derived from it; those are neighbouring models. The model is storage-neutral: SAF-T XML, XBRL GL instances, pipe-delimited audit data files, ERP tables, MongoDB documents and append-only ledgers are projections of the same semantics.
in_scope: Entry header and posting lines, their identifiers, and the balancing invariant between debits and credits
Monetary measurement: amount, direction, transaction currency, functional and reporting currency translation, rounding
Distinct time roles: document date, accounting effective date, posting date, value date, system entry (ingestion) time, approval time
Entry lifecycle from draft through posting to immutability, plus reversal, storno and correction linkage
Provenance: source system, source document reference, derivation rule, preparer, approver, batch and interface lineage
Authority and segregation of duties governing who may post what, where and when
Fiscal period assignment, period state (open, soft-closed, hard-closed) and cut-off treatment
Tax and analytical attributes carried on lines (tax code, taxable base, cost centre, project, segment, counterparty)
Validation, reconciliation to account balances, completeness of the extracted population and control totals
Audit risk signals on entries, supporting evidence, change-history and integrity controls
Access control, regulator and auditor access, retention, legal hold and lawful disposal
Export and exchange profiles (SAF-T, XBRL GL, audit data standards, statement entries) and code-list mapping
out_of_scope: Chart of accounts, account master data and derived account balances (owned by WM-ECO-015 Financial Account)
Payment initiation, clearing and settlement mechanics of a payment instruction (owned by WM-ECO-009 Payment)
Invoice and other commercial source-document content and their legal validity requirements
Financial statements, consolidation output and disclosure taxonomies
Legal entity, customer and supplier master records, including LEI issuance and KYC
Currency, unit-of-measure and country code registries as registries
Budgeting, commitment and encumbrance accounting, and management forecasts
Tax return computation and filing obligations
Consensus, cryptographic and network mechanics of distributed-ledger platforms

boundary_notes.distinction: The account owns the chart-of-accounts record and derived balances; this model owns the posting event and its balancing invariant. Account existence and status are referenced preconditions, never redefined here. Audit data and SAF-T structures likewise separate the chart of accounts and trial balance from general-ledger entries.

A payment is an instruction and a value transfer; a journal entry is its accounting representation. One payment may produce several postings in several ledgers, and a bank statement entry is the account servicer's own posting, not the customer's journal entry. Booking status and settlement finality are read from the payment side and only referenced here.

SAF-T and comparable audit files place source documents in a separate section from general-ledger entries. The entry carries a resolvable reference and a document archive number, but the legal content and format of the invoice belong to the source-document model.

Aggregation into statements, and the taxonomies used to report them, sit outside. XBRL GL provides an explicit mapping module (SRCD) to financial reporting taxonomies precisely because the two layers are distinct.
Counterparties are referenced by governed identifiers such as the ISO 17442 Legal Entity Identifier; the entry never becomes the master record for entity reference data or ownership structure.

REA models resources, economic events and agents at business level. This model deliberately covers only the accounting artifact derived from such events; duplicating resource and agent modelling here would collide with that ontology. The alignment is asserted at catalogue level only and is marked as an evidence gap.

sources.title: Guidance for the Standard Audit File - Tax, Version 2.0 (Appendix B: SAF-T Schema version 2.00)
sources.relevance: Defines the SAF-T file structure: header, master files, GeneralLedgerEntries (journal, transaction, line) and source documents, with control totals and tax information. Retrieved as PDF; structural detail corroborated by SRC-003 and SRC-013 because the PDF text layer was not machine-extractable.

sources.title: XBRL Global Ledger Taxonomy Framework 2015
sources.relevance: Normative representation of journal entries: accountingEntries/entryHeader/entryDetail, entriesType, entryNumber, postingDate and enteredDate, account and accountMainID, debitCreditCode, amount and signOfAmount, plus MUC (multi-currency), TAF (tax audit file) and SRCD (mapping to reporting taxonomies) modules.

sources.title: Audit Data Standards: General Ledger Standard
sources.relevance: Defines GL_Detail, Trial_Balance, Chart_of_Accounts, Source_Listing and Business_Unit_Listing tables, journal entry line fields, entered/effective/approved/last-modified date and actor fields, and supplemental questions and validation routines for completeness and integrity. Offered as pipe-delimited flat file or XBRL GL.

sources.title: ISO 21378:2019 Audit data collection
sources.relevance: Establishes common definitions of accounting data elements and a modular structure (Base, General Ledger, AR, Sales, AP, Purchase, Inventory, PPE) for expressing accounting information independently of the accounting or ERP system. Catalogue entry consulted; full text is paywalled, so field-level claims are not asserted from this source.

sources.title: AS 2401: Consideration of Fraud in a Financial Statement Audit
sources.relevance: Paragraphs .58-.62 require testing of journal entries and other adjustments and list characteristics of fraudulent entries: unrelated, unusual or seldom-used accounts; unusual posters; period-end and post-closing timing; missing descriptions; round numbers; accounts with significant estimates.

sources.title: 17 CFR 240.17a-4 - Records to be preserved by certain exchange members, brokers and dealers
sources.organization: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (text hosted by Cornell Legal Information Institute)
sources.relevance: Six-year retention for blotters, ledgers and journals with the first two years easily accessible; electronic recordkeeping either in non-rewriteable non-erasable (WORM) form or under a complete time-stamped audit trail preserving original and modified records with actor identity; indexing, immediate download, and third-party access undertaking or designated executive officer.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Defines full-date, full-time and date-time with mandatory seconds and an explicit time-offset of Z or +/-HH:MM, the -00:00 convention for unknown local offset, and leap-second handling. Basis for the model's timestamp rule.

sources.title: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting
sources.organization: IFRS Foundation / International Accounting Standards Board
sources.version_or_date: Issued March 2018; effective for policy development from 1 January 2020
sources.relevance: Supplies the definitions of assets, liabilities, equity, income and expenses, the recognition and derecognition criteria, measurement bases and unit-of-account concepts that determine whether and at what amount a posting may be made.

sources.title: Introducing the Legal Entity Identifier (LEI)
sources.relevance: Governed 20-character global identifier for legal entities under ISO 17442, administered by GLEIF with ROC oversight; supports the second tier of the identity priority for reporting entity and counterparty references on postings.

sources.title: ISO 20022 Message Definition Report Part 2 - Bank-to-Customer Cash Management
sources.relevance: Defines the account-servicer Entry / EntryDetails / TransactionDetails structure with EntryReference, Amount, CreditDebitIndicator (CRDT/DBIT), ReversalIndicator, Status (BOOK for booked entries), BookingDate, ValueDate, AccountServicerReference and BankTransactionCode - the interoperability anchor for transfer-derived postings.

sources.title: Principles for financial market infrastructures
sources.organization: Committee on Payment and Settlement Systems (BIS) and IOSCO
sources.relevance: Establishes settlement finality and money settlement principles governing when a transfer becomes irrevocable and unconditional, which determines whether a related posting may be treated as final rather than provisional. Landing page retrieved; principle text is in the linked PDF, so only the existence, date and subject matter are asserted.

sources.title: Companies Act 2006, section 386 (duty to keep accounting records) and section 388
sources.organization: United Kingdom Parliament / The National Archives (legislation.gov.uk)
sources.relevance: Statutory requirement for records sufficient to show and explain transactions and disclose financial position with reasonable accuracy at any time, including entries from day to day of all sums received and expended and the matters in respect of which receipt and expenditure takes place; section 388 sets 3-year (private) and 6-year (public) retention.

sources.title: Norwegian SAF-T schemas, code lists and test files
sources.version_or_date: SAF-T Financial schema versions 1.3 and 1.4, retrieved 2026-08-25
sources.relevance: Working national profile of OECD SAF-T publishing versioned schemas, standard-account code lists and conformance test files; evidence that national profiles constrain and extend the base schema and that code lists are versioned artifacts in their own right.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 15944-4:2015 Information technology - Business operational view - Part 4: Business transaction scenarios - Accounting and economic ontology
sources.relevance: Defines the accounting and economic (REA: Resource-Event-Agent) ontology for business transaction scenarios, used here only to fix the boundary between business-level economic events and the accounting artifact. Catalogue entry consulted; full text paywalled, so no field-level claims are drawn from it.

sources.title: XBRL Global Ledger: Transactional Reporting
sources.relevance: Defines XBRL GL as the system-independent record of original ledger detail, journal entries and drill-down from summary reports, including audit, consolidation and transfer use.

sources.title: Audit Focus: Journal Entries
sources.relevance: Authoritative staff reminder of journal-entry testing: controls over initiate-authorize-record-process, completeness of the population, manual versus automated origin, post-closing and fraudulent-entry characteristics.

sources.title: AS 2201: An Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting That Is Integrated with An Audit of Financial Statements
sources.version_or_date: current PCAOB auditing standard as published 2026-08-25
sources.relevance: Requires controls over journal entries and period-end adjustments, significant unusual transactions that result in late or unusual journal entries, and procedures to initiate, authorize, record and process entries in the general ledger.

sources.title: Catalogue of messages
sources.relevance: Official inventory of approved ISO 20022 message definitions, including cash-management and account-reporting messages used to report booked cash transactions.

sources.title: ISO 20022 Bank Transaction Codes - External Code Sets
sources.relevance: Harmonised bank transaction codes for bank-to-customer cash account reporting so the account owner can reconcile cash movements to sub-ledgers and processing systems.

sources.title: ISO 4217 — Currency codes
sources.relevance: Alphabetic and numeric currency codes and minor-unit exponents required to express posting amounts without ambiguity.

sources.title: Financial Industry Business Ontology (FIBO) repository
sources.relevance: Formal OWL vocabulary for financial contracts and process flows; BP domain transaction semantics are an adjacent meaning of financial transaction that must not be collapsed into a ledger posting.

sources.title: ISO 20022 Message Definitions
sources.relevance: Machine-readable message inventory and schemas for ISO 20022, including account management and other financial-message families that carry booked amounts and references.

sources.title: Transactional Reporting (Global Ledger)
sources.relevance: States that XBRL GL represents chart of accounts, journal entries and historical transactions without requiring a standardised chart of accounts.

sources.title: ISO 20022 MDR Part 1 BankToCustomer Cash Management
sources.relevance: Message definition report for bank-to-customer cash management, including BankToCustomerStatement camt.053, designed to report cash transactions between an account servicer and its customers.

bundles.name: Identity and classification of the posting
bundles.description: What this entry is, how it is named, which book it lives in and how it is typed.
bundles.rationale: Every downstream operation - validation, correction, export, audit selection - depends on being able to name the entry unambiguously and know which ledger and category it belongs to. Audit and tax file formats all begin with an entry identifier plus journal and ledger context.

layers.name: Entry and line identification
layers.description: Identifiers for the entry aggregate and its lines, their scope, and the external references that must resolve.

findings.name: Entry and posting line identification
findings.description: How the entry and each of its lines are named by the ledger of record, and which external references must resolve back to them.

questions.text: Which system of record issues this entry's authoritative identifier, and under what scheme?
How is each posting line addressed, and does that address stay stable across export and re-import?
Which external references - payment end-to-end reference, bank entry reference, source document number - must resolve back to this entry?
Over what scope and for how long is the entry identifier guaranteed unique and never reused?
answer_data: uniqueness scope (ledger, entity, fiscal year, file)

data_elements.name: Entry identifier
data_elements.description: Authoritative identifier of the entry issued by the ledger of record.

data_elements.name: Posting line identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier or ordinal of a line within the entry; unique within the entry.

data_elements.name: External reference
data_elements.description: Typed reference to a payment, statement entry or source document held in another model.

artifacts.name: Posted journal entry record
artifacts.description: The immutable record of the entry header and its balanced lines as held by the ledger of record.
media_or_form: XBRL GL entryHeader with entryDetail children
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative entry identifier issued by the ledger of record, qualified by ledger and reporting entity; line identity is entry identifier plus line number.

findings.name: Journal assignment and entry typing
findings.description: Which journal or daybook the entry belongs to and how its nature and origin are coded.

questions.text: To which journal, daybook or subledger is the entry assigned, and who governs that code list?
Was the entry keyed manually, generated by an automated interface, or produced from a recurring template?
Which transaction type or bank transaction code describes the economic nature of the posting?
May an entry's classification change after posting, and how would such a change be recorded?

data_elements.name: Journal identifier
data_elements.description: Code of the journal, daybook or subledger holding the entry.

data_elements.name: Entry origin category
data_elements.description: Whether the entry is manual, interfaced, recurring, adjusting, closing, reversing or consolidating.

data_elements.name: Bank transaction code
data_elements.description: Account-servicer classification of a transfer-derived entry (domain, family, sub-family).

artifacts.name: Entry type and journal code list
artifacts.description: Versioned list of journal codes, entry origin categories and transaction type codes in force for a ledger.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Code list namespace plus issuing authority plus version; individual codes identified by scheme-qualified code value.

layers.name: Ledger and framework context
layers.description: The book, reporting entity, accounting framework and functional currency that give the posting meaning.

findings.name: Ledger, entity and accounting framework context
findings.description: Which book the entry lives in, which legal entity owns it, and under which framework and functional currency it is measured.

questions.text: In which ledger or book - statutory, tax, management or parallel framework ledger - is this entry recorded?
Which legal entity and business unit own the ledger, and by which governed identifier are they named?
Which accounting framework and jurisdiction govern the ledger, and what is its functional currency?
When one economic event is posted to several parallel ledgers, how are those postings linked to each other?

data_elements.name: Ledger identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the book of account in which the entry is recorded.

data_elements.name: Reporting entity reference
data_elements.description: Governed identifier of the legal entity owning the ledger.

data_elements.name: Functional currency
data_elements.description: Currency in which the ledger measures results.

artifacts.name: Ledger definition profile
artifacts.description: Declaration of a ledger's purpose, owning entity, framework, functional currency, fiscal calendar and code lists.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Ledger identifier qualified by reporting entity identifier; version-stamped on each change of framework or currency.

bundles.name: Composition, balancing and measurement
bundles.description: How the entry is built from lines, why it must balance, and how each line's amount is measured.
bundles.rationale: The balancing invariant and the monetary measurement of each line are the defining properties that separate a journal entry from any other record of an event; audit files carry explicit debit and credit amounts and control totals precisely to make the invariant checkable.

layers.name: Posting structure
layers.description: Header-to-line composition, the balancing invariant and the analytical dimensions carried by lines.

findings.name: Header-to-line composition
findings.description: What constitutes a complete entry, which attributes sit on the header and which repeat on each line.

questions.text: What is the minimum and maximum set of posting lines that constitutes a complete entry?
answer_data: maximum line count or unbounded flag

questions.text: Which account does each line debit or credit, and how is that account reference resolved and validated?
Which attributes belong on the entry header and which must be repeated on every line?
answer_data: attributes permitted at both levels with precedence rule

data_elements.name: Posting line
data_elements.description: One debit or credit against a single account, with amount, direction and qualifying attributes.

data_elements.name: Account reference
data_elements.description: Reference from a line to the account it posts against, resolved in the account model.

data_elements.name: Entry description
data_elements.description: Narrative explaining the entry; a separate line-level narrative may also exist.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Composition is a structural property of the entry record already captured by art-posted-entry-record; it produces no separate artifact of its own. Header and line attributes are inline data within that record, and the account it points to is an artifact owned by WM-ECO-015.

findings.name: Balancing invariant and control totals
findings.description: At which level debits must equal credits, which control totals travel with a batch, and what happens on imbalance.

questions.text: At which level - line set, entry, batch, ledger or currency - must debits equal credits, and to what tolerance?
Which control totals accompany a batch or export, and how are they recomputed on receipt?
What happens to an entry that fails the balancing test at capture, at posting and after export?
answer_data: rejection or quarantine rule per stage

data_elements.name: Total debit
data_elements.description: Sum of debit amounts asserted for an entry, batch or export.

data_elements.name: Total credit
data_elements.description: Sum of credit amounts asserted for an entry, batch or export.

data_elements.name: Number of entries
data_elements.description: Count of entries asserted in a batch or export header.

artifacts.name: Batch control total record
artifacts.description: Header assertion of entry count, total debit and total credit for a batch or exported period.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Batch or export identifier issued by the producing system, plus the ledger identifier and asserted period; never identified by the file's date alone.

findings.name: Analytical dimensions on postings
findings.description: The non-account qualifiers a line may carry and the rules that make them mandatory.

questions.text: Which analytical dimensions - cost centre, project, segment, counterparty, product - may qualify a posting line?
Which dimension values are mandatory for which account ranges, and who sets that rule?
When a line carries a non-monetary quantity or unit, how is it recorded alongside the monetary amount?

data_elements.name: Analytical dimension value
data_elements.description: Typed qualifier on a line, such as cost centre, project, segment or counterparty.

data_elements.name: Line quantity
data_elements.description: Non-monetary quantity and unit associated with a posting line.

data_elements.name: Counterparty reference
data_elements.description: Customer, supplier or other counterparty associated with the line.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Dimension values are inline coded attributes on the posting line; the authoritative value sets are code-list artifacts already governed by art-entry-type-code-list and by the dimension owner's own model, so no additional artifact is created here.

layers.name: Monetary measurement
layers.description: Amount, direction, currency, translation to reporting currencies and tax attributes.

findings.name: Amount, direction and currency of a posting
findings.description: How a line's value and its debit or credit sense are represented, with scale, rounding and edge cases.

questions.text: Is direction represented by an explicit debit or credit indicator, by a signed amount, or by both, and which representation is authoritative?
In which currency is the line amount denominated, and how is that currency code governed?
What scale and rounding rule apply to the amount, and where is any rounding difference posted?
Are zero-value and negative-value postings permitted, and what do they mean here?

data_elements.name: Line amount
data_elements.description: Non-negative magnitude of the posting in the transaction currency, stored as an exact decimal.

data_elements.name: Credit/debit indicator
data_elements.description: Explicit direction of the posting, corresponding to debitCreditCode or CRDT/DBIT.

data_elements.name: Transaction currency
data_elements.description: Currency in which the line amount is denominated.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Amount, direction and currency are atomic inline values on the posting line inside art-posted-entry-record; separating them into an artifact would fragment the record that must be verified as a whole.

findings.name: Multi-currency translation and rate provenance
findings.description: Additional currency amounts stored on a line, the rate used, and how later revaluations link back.

questions.text: Which additional currency amounts - functional, group reporting or tax - are stored on the line?
Which exchange rate, rate date and rate source were applied, and who published that rate?
How are later revaluation or translation adjustments linked back to the original posting?

data_elements.name: Reporting currency amount
data_elements.description: Translated amount in the functional or group reporting currency, with its currency role.

data_elements.name: Exchange rate applied
data_elements.description: Rate value, rate type and rate date used to translate the line amount.

data_elements.name: Exchange rate source
data_elements.description: Publisher of the applied rate, such as a central bank or contractual rate provider.

artifacts.name: Applied exchange rate table
artifacts.description: Versioned set of rates, rate types and effective dates used for translating postings.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Rate source identifier plus rate type plus effective date range plus publication sequence; the effective date is an attribute of the rate, not the identifier of the table.

findings.name: Tax attributes carried by postings
findings.description: Tax codes, taxable base, tax amounts and tax point dates carried at line level for audit and tax reporting.

questions.text: Which tax code, tax type and tax jurisdiction apply to the line, and against which taxable base?
How are taxable base, tax amount and any non-deductible portion recorded as separate values?
Which date determines the tax point, and how does it differ from the posting date?

data_elements.name: Tax code
data_elements.description: Jurisdiction-specific tax classification applied to the line.

data_elements.name: Tax amount
data_elements.description: Tax value attributable to the line, alongside its taxable base.

artifacts.name: Tax code table and mapping
artifacts.description: Versioned table of tax codes, rates, jurisdictions and their mapping to statutory reporting categories.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Jurisdiction plus issuing authority plus code list version; each code identified by scheme-qualified code value with validity period as an attribute.

bundles.name: Time, period and lifecycle
bundles.description: Distinct time roles, fiscal period placement, state transitions, correction and settlement finality.
bundles.rationale: Journal entries carry several genuinely different dates, and the audit consequences of confusing them are severe: period assignment drives reporting, capture time drives audit trail, value date drives cash availability, and finality determines whether a posting is provisional.

layers.name: Time semantics
layers.description: The separate date and timestamp roles on an entry and the fiscal period they resolve to.

findings.name: Distinct date and timestamp roles
findings.description: Which dates and instants an entry carries, how event time is separated from capture time, and how each is formatted.

questions.text: Which distinct date and timestamp roles does this entry carry, and what does each one mean?
How is the accounting event time separated from the system capture or ingestion time on this record?
In what format and offset are instants stored, and how are pure accounting dates distinguished from instants?
Under whose authority may an entry be dated earlier than its capture time, and how is that flagged?

data_elements.name: Accounting effective date
data_elements.description: Calendar date determining the accounting period of the entry.

data_elements.name: Posting date
data_elements.description: Date on which the entry was posted to the ledger, distinct from its effective date.

data_elements.name: System entry timestamp
data_elements.description: Instant at which the record was captured by the system, recorded separately from event time.

data_elements.name: Value date
data_elements.description: Date on which value becomes available or ceases to be available for a transfer-derived posting.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Date and timestamp roles are inline scalar attributes of the entry record and its lines. They are governed by the service-layer timestamp rule rather than by a separate artifact; creating one would detach time semantics from the record whose integrity they qualify.

findings.name: Fiscal period, period state and cut-off
findings.description: How the entry resolves to a fiscal period, whether that period accepts postings, and how cut-off adjustments are marked.

questions.text: To which fiscal year and accounting period is the entry assigned, and by which rule?
answer_data: assignment rule and fiscal calendar reference

questions.text: Is the target period open, soft-closed or hard-closed, and who may post into each state?
How are cut-off, accrual and post-closing adjustments identified and separated from routine entries?

data_elements.name: Fiscal period
data_elements.description: Fiscal year and period to which the entry is assigned.

data_elements.name: Period state
data_elements.description: Whether the period is open, soft-closed or hard-closed for posting.

artifacts.name: Period close record
artifacts.description: Record that a fiscal period has been closed, by whom, with which balances and which residual open items.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Ledger identifier plus fiscal year and period label plus close sequence number issued by the ledger of record.

layers.name: Lifecycle, correction and finality
layers.description: State model up to immutability, correction mechanics, and the finality of transfer-derived postings.

findings.name: Entry states and the immutability point
findings.description: Permitted states and transitions, where the record becomes immutable, and how provisional postings are marked.

questions.text: What are the permitted states of an entry and the legal transitions between them?
At which state does the entry become immutable, and exactly which fields may no longer change?
answer_data: fields still mutable with audit trail

questions.text: How is a pending or provisional posting distinguished from a booked one by downstream consumers?
What becomes of drafts that are never posted, and for how long are they kept?

data_elements.name: Entry state
data_elements.description: Current lifecycle state of the entry, such as draft, approved, posted or reversed.

data_elements.name: Booking status
data_elements.description: Whether the posting is booked or still pending, for transfer-derived entries.

findings.inline_only_rationale: State is an attribute of the entry record, and every transition is captured by art-change-audit-log. A separate lifecycle artifact would duplicate the audit trail that regulation already requires to be the authoritative history.

findings.name: Reversal, storno and correction linkage
findings.description: How a posted entry is corrected without being altered, and how the corrective chain is made traceable.

questions.text: Is correction made by reversing entry, storno, or negative posting, and which method is authoritative in this ledger?
How are the original entry, the reversing entry and any replacement entry linked in both directions?
Into which period is a reversal posted when the original period is already closed?
Who may authorise a reversal, and what reason code and evidence must accompany it?

data_elements.name: Reversal indicator
data_elements.description: Flag marking the entry or line as a reversal of a previous posting.

data_elements.name: Corrected entry reference
data_elements.description: Reference from a corrective entry to the entry it reverses or replaces.

data_elements.name: Correction reason code
data_elements.description: Coded justification for the reversal or correction.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A reversal is itself an instance of art-posted-entry-record; the corrective relationship is inline reference data linking two entry records. Introducing a distinct correction artifact would create a second, competing record of a fact the ledger must already hold.

findings.name: Booking status and settlement finality for transfers
findings.description: Whether the underlying transfer is final, when it became irrevocable, and how provisional postings are unwound.

questions.text: What booking status does the underlying transfer carry, and does this posting depend on that status?
At which moment does the transfer become irrevocable and unconditional, and how is that moment evidenced?
answer_data: finality rule or system rulebook reference

questions.text: How are provisional postings unwound when a transfer is returned, recalled or rejected?

data_elements.name: Settlement finality timestamp
data_elements.description: Instant at which the underlying transfer became irrevocable and unconditional.

data_elements.name: Settlement system reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the payment or securities settlement system whose rules define finality.

artifacts.name: Account statement entry
artifacts.description: Account servicer's booked entry advice used as external evidence for a transfer-derived posting.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Account servicer reference or entry reference issued by the account servicer, qualified by the servicing institution identifier and statement sequence number.

findings.name: Reversals, corrections and period-end adjustments
findings.description: Rare but required cases include auto-reversing accruals, prior-period corrections, consolidating and reclassification adjustments, late or unusual entries, and top-side adjustments that may not appear as formal journal entries in the general ledger.

questions.text: Is this entry a reversal, a correcting entry, a prior-period restatement, or an auto-reversing accrual, and which original entry does it supersede?
Is this adjustment a consolidating, combination, reclassification or other top-side item that is not reflected as a formal journal entry in the general ledger?
Was the entry recorded at period end or post-close, to seldom-used accounts, by an unusual preparer, or with round-number or unexplained characteristics?

data_elements.name: Adjustment class
data_elements.description: Reversal, correction, auto-reversing accrual, restatement, consolidation, reclassification or top-side.

data_elements.name: Original entry identifier
data_elements.description: Reference to the entry being reversed or corrected.

data_elements.name: Top-side flag
data_elements.description: Whether the adjustment is outside formal general-ledger journal entries.

data_elements.name: Post-close flag
data_elements.description: Whether the entry was recorded after books were closed.

artifacts.name: Reversal or adjusting voucher
artifacts.description: Document that reverses or adjusts a prior posted entry, including link to the original.
artifacts.identity_strategy: New journal number for the reversing or adjusting document; original number stored as a reference, never reused as the identity of the reversal.

bundles.name: Provenance, authority and control
bundles.description: Where the entry came from, who made and approved it, what may not be changed, and who was entitled to act.
bundles.rationale: Recordkeeping regulation and auditing standards both treat the answer to 'who did this, from what source, and could it have been altered' as the core control question for postings; the audit trail is itself a regulated object.

layers.name: Provenance and audit trail
layers.description: Source derivation, actor attribution and the protected change history of the record.

findings.name: Source system, source event and derivation rule
findings.description: Which system and business event produced the entry, under which posting rule, and whether it can be re-derived.

questions.text: Which source system, interface and batch produced this entry?
Which source document or business event does the entry represent, and how is that reference resolved?
Which posting rule, template or algorithm derived the lines from the source event, and in which version?
Can the entry be re-derived deterministically from its source, and would re-derivation mint a new identifier?

data_elements.name: Source system identifier
data_elements.description: System that originated the entry, as recorded on the entry header.

data_elements.name: Source document reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the invoice, payment or other source document evidencing the entry.

data_elements.name: Posting rule reference
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the rule or template that derived the lines.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The source document is an artifact owned by the invoice or payment model; duplicating it here would create a second custodial copy with divergent retention. This finding contributes only the resolvable reference and the derivation metadata, which are inline attributes of the entry record.

findings.name: Actor attribution and approval
findings.description: Who prepared, approved and released the entry, and how non-human actors are tied to accountable owners.

questions.text: Who entered the entry, under which account, and on whose behalf?
Who approved or released the entry, when, and under which approval rule?
How are entries created by service accounts, robots or scheduled jobs attributed to an accountable human owner?

data_elements.name: Entered by
data_elements.description: Identity of the actor who created the entry.

data_elements.name: Approved by
data_elements.description: Identity of the actor who approved or released the entry, with approval time.

artifacts.name: Approval and release record
artifacts.description: Evidence of who approved an entry, when, under which rule and against which limits.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Entry identifier plus approval step identifier plus approver identity; approval instant is an attribute, never the identifier.

findings.name: Change history, immutability and integrity
findings.description: What the audit trail must capture, how originals are preserved, and how integrity of a posted entry is proven.

questions.text: What does the change record capture for every modification or deletion attempt on a posted record?
How are both the original and the modified version of a record preserved and retrievable?
What control proves that a posted entry has not been altered since posting?
Is the record held in non-rewriteable non-erasable form or under an audit-trail alternative, and who attests to that?

data_elements.name: Change event
data_elements.description: Recorded modification or deletion attempt with actor, timestamp, and prior and new values.

data_elements.name: Record integrity hash
data_elements.description: Digest over the canonical form of the posted entry used to detect alteration.

artifacts.name: Change audit log
artifacts.description: Complete time-stamped trail of creations, modifications and deletions affecting entries, preserving originals.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Log stream identifier plus monotonic sequence number issued by the recording system; each record keyed by the affected entry identifier and sequence position.

layers.name: Authority and accounting policy
layers.description: Who is entitled to post, and under which recognition and measurement basis the posting is justified.

findings.name: Posting authority, limits and segregation of duties
findings.description: Entitlement to post to given accounts, periods and amounts, and the prohibited combinations of rights.

questions.text: Who is permitted to post to which accounts, periods, amounts and ledgers?
Which combinations of preparation, approval and posting rights are prohibited for a single actor?
Which decision record authorises an automated interface to post without human approval, and how is it revoked?
answer_data: scope and limits of the mandate

data_elements.name: Posting authority scope
data_elements.description: Account, period, ledger and amount boundaries within which an actor may post.

data_elements.name: Segregation of duties rule
data_elements.description: Declaration of right combinations that may not be held by one actor.

artifacts.name: Posting authority matrix
artifacts.description: Authoritative mapping of roles to permitted accounts, periods, amount limits and prohibited right combinations.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Ledger identifier plus policy identifier plus version; effective period recorded as an attribute of each policy version.

findings.name: Recognition, derecognition and measurement basis
findings.description: Why the posting is permitted under the applicable framework and on what basis its amount was determined.

questions.text: Which recognition criterion under the applicable framework triggers this posting?
answer_data: element affected (asset, liability, equity, income, expense)

questions.text: On which measurement basis is the amount determined, and what is the unit of account?
Which event derecognises the asset or liability, and which posting records that removal?
Does the amount rest on an estimate or judgement, and how is that flagged for audit attention?

data_elements.name: Financial statement element category
data_elements.description: Whether the line affects an asset, liability, equity, income or expense.

data_elements.name: Measurement basis
data_elements.description: Basis on which the amount was measured, such as historical cost or a current value basis.

data_elements.name: Estimate indicator
data_elements.description: Flag that the amount involves significant estimation or judgement.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The accounting policy and framework text are artifacts of the reporting-framework and policy models; this finding contributes only the per-entry classification and basis attributes plus a citation reference, which are inline data on the entry.

findings.name: Initiate, authorize, record and process
findings.description: Controls must cover initiation, authorization, recording and processing of both automated and manual journal entries in the general ledger, subsidiary ledgers and other IT systems. Segregation of duties and dual control are expected except where a documented compensating control exists.

questions.text: Who initiated this entry and who authorized it, and are those persons different under the segregation-of-duties rule?
Through which IT systems or interfaces was the entry recorded and processed, including subledger feeds?
Which roles may read the entry or its supporting evidence, and which fields are restricted as personal or commercially sensitive?
Was any control overridden, and what management or system override evidence exists?

data_elements.name: Initiator identifier
data_elements.description: Person or system that initiated the entry.

data_elements.name: Authorizer identifier
data_elements.description: Person or system that authorized posting.

data_elements.name: Segregation of duties satisfied
data_elements.description: Whether initiator and authorizer are distinct as required.

data_elements.name: Control override flag
data_elements.description: Whether a control was overridden for this entry.

artifacts.name: Authorization record
artifacts.description: Approval artefact or system workflow step proving authorization before post.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by authorization event identifier linked to the journal number.

bundles.name: Validation, assurance and audit signals
bundles.description: Rules that make an entry acceptable, checks that make a population credible, and signals that make it suspicious.
bundles.rationale: Audit data standards pair field definitions with validation routines and completeness questions, and auditing standards require entries to be tested against defined risk characteristics; both are part of the operating surface an agent must serve.

layers.name: Validation and reconciliation
layers.description: Acceptance rules for a single entry and assurance over the completeness of a population.

findings.name: Structural and referential validation
findings.description: Which fields are required, which references must resolve and be active, and how schema conformance is judged.

questions.text: Which fields are mandatory for an entry to be accepted, and which are conditionally mandatory?
Which referenced objects - account, period, currency, tax code, counterparty - must exist and be active at posting time?
Against which schema version is an incoming entry validated, and what happens to unknown fields?

data_elements.name: Validation result
data_elements.description: Outcome of applying the rule set to an entry, with rule identifiers and severities.

data_elements.name: Schema version applied
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the schema or profile the entry was validated against.

artifacts.name: Validation rule set
artifacts.description: Versioned catalogue of structural, referential and business rules applied to entries, with severities.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Rule set namespace plus version identifier, bound to a named schema or export profile version.

findings.name: Reconciliation and population completeness
findings.description: Whether postings agree to balances, whether the sequence is intact, and who attests that the extraction is complete.

questions.text: Does the sum of postings agree to opening and closing account balances for the period?
Are there gaps or duplicates in the entry sequence, and how is each one explained?
How do subledger postings tie out to the general ledger control accounts?
Who attests that the extracted population of entries is complete for the stated scope and period?

data_elements.name: Reconciliation difference
data_elements.description: Residual difference between posting movement and balance change, with its explanation.

data_elements.name: Population scope statement
data_elements.description: Ledger, entity, period and filter criteria defining the extracted population.

artifacts.name: Reconciliation and completeness report
artifacts.description: Report tying postings to balances, listing sequence exceptions and recording the completeness attestation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Ledger identifier plus scope statement plus run sequence number issued by the reconciling system; run instant is an attribute.

layers.name: Audit risk signals and evidence
layers.description: Characteristics that make an entry worth investigating, and the supporting documentation behind it.

findings.name: Journal entry risk indicators
findings.description: The account, actor, timing and narrative characteristics used to select entries for fraud-focused testing.

questions.text: Does the entry touch unrelated, unusual or seldom-used account combinations?
Was the entry posted by someone who does not normally post to those accounts?
Was the entry recorded at period end, after close, or outside normal business hours?
Does the entry carry a meaningful description, or is it blank, round-numbered or templated?

data_elements.name: Risk indicator flag
data_elements.description: Named risk characteristic detected on an entry, with the rule that raised it.

data_elements.name: Risk score
data_elements.description: Composite score assigned to an entry by the selection routine.

artifacts.name: Entry risk scoring report
artifacts.description: Output of applying risk-indicator rules to a population, with selected entries and rationale.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Population scope plus rule set version plus run sequence number; the report references entries by their master-system identifiers.

findings.name: Supporting evidence and documentation
findings.description: Which documents substantiate the entry, how much is required, and how the link is protected.

questions.text: Which supporting documents are attached or referenced, and where are they held?
What level of supporting evidence is required for each entry type and amount band?
How is the link between entry and evidence protected against substitution, breakage or loss?

data_elements.name: Evidence reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to a supporting document, including its archive number where one exists.

data_elements.name: Evidence digest
data_elements.description: Digest of the referenced evidence captured at attachment time.

artifacts.name: Supporting evidence attachment
artifacts.description: Stored or referenced document substantiating the entry, with its digest and custody metadata.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Document archive number or repository identifier issued by the custodian, bound to the entry identifier and verified by content digest.

bundles.name: Access, retention and exchange
bundles.description: Who may see the entry, how long it must survive, and how it crosses system and jurisdictional boundaries.
bundles.rationale: Postings are simultaneously confidential commercial data, statutorily retained records, and mandatory disclosures to auditors and tax authorities; these obligations pull in different directions and must be modelled explicitly rather than assumed.

layers.name: Access and confidentiality
layers.description: Default and privileged read rights, mandated third-party access, and personal data carried inside entries.

findings.name: Access, mandated disclosure and personal data in entries
findings.description: Who may read entries, what auditors and authorities may demand, and how personal data inside entries is handled.

questions.text: Who may read a posted entry by default, and at what granularity - header, line, amount, narrative?
Which roles may see restricted amounts, counterparties or narratives, and under what conditions?
What obligation exists to furnish entries promptly to auditors, tax authorities or regulators, and through whom?
Which personal data can appear in entry narratives, counterparty fields and attachments?
How is an erasure request reconciled with statutory retention and audit-trail immutability?
answer_data: record of the decision and its authoriser

data_elements.name: Confidentiality classification
data_elements.description: Sensitivity class assigned to the entry or specific fields.

data_elements.name: Access event
data_elements.description: Recorded read, export or disclosure action with actor, scope and timestamp.

data_elements.name: Personal data field marker
data_elements.description: Marker identifying a field that may carry personal data about a natural person.

artifacts.name: Access and disclosure log
artifacts.description: Log of who read, exported or disclosed entries, at what scope and under which authority.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Log stream identifier plus monotonic sequence; each record keyed to the accessing actor and the entry or population identifier accessed.

layers.name: Retention and disposal
layers.description: How long entries and their evidence must survive, in what accessibility tier, and how disposal is proven.

findings.name: Retention schedule, legal hold and lawful disposal
findings.description: The applicable retention clock, accessibility obligations during it, hold mechanics and evidence of disposal.

questions.text: For how long must this entry and its evidence be retained, under which rule, and when does the clock start?
Which portion of the retention period requires immediately accessible storage rather than archival storage?
How is a legal hold applied to entries, and what does it suspend?
What record proves lawful disposal at the end of the retention period?

data_elements.name: Retention rule reference
data_elements.description: Citation of the statutory or contractual rule fixing the retention duration.

data_elements.name: Retention expiry date
data_elements.description: Date on which the retention obligation lapses, derived from the clock start and duration.

data_elements.name: Legal hold reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of a hold suspending disposal for the entry or population.

artifacts.name: Retention and legal hold register
artifacts.description: Register of retention classes, expiry calculations, active holds and completed disposals for ledger records.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Retention class identifier plus governing rule citation plus version; individual holds identified by hold identifier issued by the records custodian.

layers.name: Exchange profiles and mapping
layers.description: The formats entries must be delivered in and the code-list mappings and conflicts those formats impose.

findings.name: Export profiles, mapping and profile conflicts
findings.description: Which exchange profile applies, what it cannot carry, how local codes map to standard ones, and which profile wins on conflict.

questions.text: Which exchange profile does the receiving authority or auditor require, and in which version?
Which model fields have no home in the target profile, and how is that loss recorded?
What population, period and entity scope does an export assert, and how is that asserted in the file header?
How are local account numbers mapped to standard or statutory account codes for the profile?
Where do required profiles disagree in semantics, and which one prevails?

data_elements.name: Export profile identifier
data_elements.description: Name and version of the exchange profile used for a delivery.

data_elements.name: Account code mapping
data_elements.description: Mapping from a local account code to a standard or statutory account code.

data_elements.name: Unmapped field record
data_elements.description: Model field with no counterpart in the target profile, with its handling decision.

artifacts.name: Audit or tax file export
artifacts.description: Delivered file containing header, master data, entries and control totals in a named profile version.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Producing system identifier plus ledger plus asserted period plus monotonic export sequence number; content digest recorded for integrity, filename dates never used as identity.

artifacts.name: Code and account mapping table
artifacts.description: Versioned mapping from local codes to standard account, tax and transaction code lists required by profiles.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Source code list plus target code list plus mapping version, each issued under a named owning authority.

functions.name: Draft a posting
functions.description: Create an unposted entry with header context and candidate lines, derived from a source event or entered manually.
inputs: proposed lines with account, direction, amount, currency
outputs: draft entry with assigned draft identifier
preconditions: ledger profile resolved
target accounts exist and are active
preparer holds capture rights for the ledger
effects: draft record created in mutable state
change audit log opened for the draft
no effect on account balances

functions.name: Validate an entry
functions.description: Apply structural, referential, balancing and business rules to an entry and report severities.
outputs: validation result set with rule identifiers and severities
preconditions: rule set version resolvable
referenced code lists and accounts retrievable at the entry's effective date
effects: validation results attached to the entry
blocking failures prevent transition to posted

functions.name: Post an entry to the ledger
functions.description: Commit a validated, authorised entry to the ledger of record and make it immutable.
outputs: posted entry with authoritative master-system identifier
preconditions: debits equal credits at the declared balancing scope
target period is open for the posting role
approver differs from preparer where segregation rules require it
effects: entry becomes immutable except through reversal
account balances move
integrity hash and audit trail entry written

functions.name: Reverse or correct a posted entry
functions.description: Create a linked reversing or replacement entry rather than altering the original record.
preconditions: original entry is in posted state
authoriser holds reversal rights
target period is open or a prior-period adjustment route is authorised
effects: original record left unaltered
reversing and replacement entries posted and linked
correction reason recorded in the audit trail

functions.name: Translate a posting to reporting currencies
functions.description: Derive functional or group reporting amounts for a line from a governed exchange rate.
outputs: applied rate with its source and date
preconditions: rate exists for the currency pair at the applicable rate date
rounding rule declared for the target currency
effects: translated amounts and rate provenance stored on the line
rounding difference routed to the declared account

functions.name: Attach supporting evidence
functions.description: Bind a supporting document to an entry with a digest and custody metadata.
preconditions: evidence sufficiency policy resolved for the entry type and amount band
custodian retention obligations at least match the entry's
effects: evidence link recorded and digest stored
broken-link detection scope extended to the new link

functions.name: Reconcile postings to balances
functions.description: Verify that posting movements explain the change in account balances for a scope and period, and analyse sequence integrity.
preconditions: population extraction complete for the declared scope
opening balances agreed to the prior period close
effects: reconciliation report produced and retained
unexplained differences raised as exceptions

functions.name: Screen entries for risk indicators
functions.description: Score a population of entries against fraud-risk characteristics and select entries for testing.
outputs: risk flags and scores per entry
preconditions: population completeness attested
actor posting history available for profiling
effects: risk scoring report produced
selected entries queued for evidence inspection

functions.name: Close an accounting period
functions.description: Transition a fiscal period to a closed state and record the closing balances and residual items.
preconditions: all draft entries for the period resolved or explicitly carried forward
reconciliation completed for the period
effects: period state changed to closed
further postings restricted to authorised post-closing routes
close event written to the audit trail

functions.name: Export an audit or tax file
functions.description: Produce a profile-conformant export of a declared entry population with control totals and mapping applied.
inputs: code and account mapping table version
preconditions: mapping table covers all codes present in the population
profile version accepted by the receiving authority
population completeness attested
effects: export artifact produced with content digest
export event logged including scope and requester
unmapped fields recorded as a known loss

functions.name: Grant scoped auditor or authority access
functions.description: Provision time-bounded, scope-limited read or export access for an auditor, tax authority or regulator.
inputs: requesting party identity and authority basis
outputs: access grant with scope and expiry
access log entries for every exercised right
preconditions: authority basis verified
scope no broader than the stated obligation
confidentiality and personal data controls applied to the scope
effects: grant issued and recorded
all reads and exports under the grant logged
grant expires automatically at the declared time

functions.name: Apply or release a legal hold
functions.description: Suspend or resume disposal for a defined population of entries and their evidence.
preconditions: population scope resolvable to entry identifiers
hold authority verified
effects: disposal suspended for the scope regardless of retention expiry
hold and release events written to the audit trail

functions.name: Authorize journal entry
functions.description: Record the authorizer distinct from the initiator and attach the authorization event required before posting.
preconditions: Entry exists in a pre-posted state
Authorizer is permitted for the book and amount
effects: Attaches an authorization artefact
May block posting if segregation of duties fails

functions.name: Reject or exception-post to closed period
functions.description: Block posting to a closed period unless a documented exception grant exists for adjusting entries.
preconditions: Period status is known for the book
effects: Prevents unauthorized closed-period posting
Records exception use when a grant is consumed

functions.name: Classify and reconcile a bank-booked entry
functions.description: Apply an ISO 20022 bank transaction code to a servicer-booked cash entry so it can be routed to the correct sub-ledger counterpart journal.
preconditions: Entry carries or can be assigned a bank transaction code
Target sub-ledger accounts are known
effects: Does not itself balance the books
Feeds a subsequent balanced posting

composition.purpose: The account is the container that holds postings; this model supplies the postings and takes account identity, status and balance semantics from the parent rather than redefining them.
A payment produces one or more postings; the entry references the payment and reads its booking status and finality rather than modelling instruction or clearing mechanics.

composition.target: Invoice / commercial source document model (sibling, identifier not yet assigned)
composition.purpose: Supplies the evidencing document referenced by the entry, kept in a separate section in audit file formats and under its own custody and retention.

composition.target: Party / legal entity model (counterparty and reporting entity)
composition.purpose: Resolves reporting entity and counterparty references through governed identifiers such as the ISO 17442 Legal Entity Identifier.
Supplies governed currency codes, minor units and unit-of-measure codes used by line amounts and quantities.

composition.target: Fiscal calendar and accounting period model
composition.purpose: Defines fiscal years, period boundaries and period states that the entry's effective date resolves against.

composition.target: Records retention and legal hold mixin
composition.purpose: Contributes retention class, expiry calculation, accessibility tier and hold semantics rather than duplicating them inside the entry model.
Contributes actor identity, delegation and entitlement structures used by preparer, approver and posting-authority findings.

composition.target: OECD Standard Audit File - Tax, Version 2.0
composition.purpose: Alignment target for export structure, control totals and the separation of master files, general ledger entries and source documents. National profiles constrain and extend it; conformance is asserted only per delivered profile version.
Alignment target for entry header and detail representation, multi-currency handling and explicit mapping to financial reporting taxonomies.

composition.target: AICPA Audit Data Standards - General Ledger Standard and ISO 21378 audit data collection
composition.purpose: Alignment targets for system-independent field definitions, actor and date fields, and validation and completeness routines used by auditors.

composition.target: ISO 20022 Bank-to-Customer Cash Management message definitions
composition.purpose: Alignment target for account servicer entry semantics: credit/debit indicator, reversal indicator, booking status, booking date and value date, and bank transaction codes.

composition.target: IFRS Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting
composition.purpose: Supplies element definitions, recognition and derecognition criteria and measurement bases that justify whether and at what amount a posting may be made.
Boundary alignment separating business-level economic events, resources and agents from the accounting artifact modelled here. Asserted at catalogue level only and flagged as an evidence gap.

composition.target: Audit engagement and assurance evidence model
