data_elements.name: Party record snapshot reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the governing party record and the version observed at issue time.

artifacts.name: Party role snapshot
artifacts.description: Immutable capture of each party's asserted name, identifiers, address and electronic address as carried on the issued document, with a link to the governing party record version.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by document authoritative identifier plus role code; linked to the party's master-system identifier where one exists.

layers.name: Line items, item identification and pricing
layers.description: The billed detail: line structure, what is being identified and classified, and how price, allowance and charge combine into line amounts.

findings.name: Invoice line structure and line-level scoping
findings.description: An invoice line groups a billed quantity, a unit of measure, a net amount, a tax category assignment and optional line-level period and references. Lines are the unit at which matching, dispute and partial credit operate, so line identity must be stable and referenceable from other documents.

questions.text: How is an individual invoice line identified so that another document can reference exactly that line?
answer_data: Line identifier value and its uniqueness scope
Referencing convention used by credit notes and responses
Sub-line identification scheme where composite items are used

questions.text: What quantity and unit of measure does the line assert, and from which code list is the unit drawn?
answer_data: Unit of measure code and code list version
Rounding or precision rule applied to the quantity

questions.text: How is the line net amount derived from price, quantity, allowances and charges?
What line-level period and external references does the line carry, and when are they required rather than optional?
answer_data: Line invoicing period start and end
Objects such as document, receipt or contract references at line level

data_elements.name: Invoice line identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the line, unique within the document.

data_elements.name: Invoiced quantity
data_elements.description: Quantity billed on the line, with its unit of measure code.

data_elements.name: Line net amount
data_elements.description: Net amount of the line, exclusive of tax, after line allowances and charges.

data_elements.name: Line invoicing period
data_elements.description: Period covered by the individual line where it differs from the document period.

data_elements.name: Order line reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the corresponding line of the purchase order.

artifacts.name: Invoice line detail set
artifacts.description: The complete ordered set of invoice lines with their identifiers, quantities, amounts, tax assignments and references, addressable as a unit for matching and partial credit.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by document authoritative identifier; each member keyed by document identifier plus line identifier.

findings.name: Item identification, classification and attributes
findings.description: A line identifies what was supplied through free-text name and description, party-scoped item identifiers, standard item identifiers from registered schemes, classification codes and item attributes. Multiple identification schemes may coexist and may disagree, so precedence and scheme qualification must be explicit.

questions.text: Which item identifiers are asserted for this line and which one is authoritative when they disagree?
answer_data: Seller, buyer, manufacturer and standard item identifiers with schemes

questions.text: Is the item name and description sufficient to satisfy the legal requirement to state the nature and extent of the supply?
answer_data: Assessment against the governing particulars requirement
Remediation where the description is insufficient

questions.text: Which classification codes are attached to the item and from which classification systems and versions?
answer_data: Purpose of each classification (statistical, tax, procurement)
Rule governing whether classification is required

questions.text: What item attributes and origin information are carried, and which of them affect tax or regulatory treatment?
answer_data: Attributes with tax or regulatory consequence

data_elements.name: Item name
data_elements.description: Short name identifying the supplied good or service.

data_elements.name: Standard item identifier
data_elements.description: Item identifier from a registered global scheme, with the scheme identifier.

data_elements.name: Party-scoped item identifier
data_elements.description: Seller, buyer or manufacturer item identifier valid only within that party's namespace.

data_elements.name: Item classification code
data_elements.description: Classification code with its classification system identifier and version.

data_elements.name: Item country of origin
data_elements.description: Country code identifying the origin of the supplied item.

artifacts.name: Item identification block
artifacts.description: Per-line block capturing all asserted item identifiers with their schemes, classifications, attributes and the declared precedence between competing identifier schemes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by document authoritative identifier plus line identifier; item-level linkage uses the authoritative item identifier where one exists.

findings.name: Prices, allowances and charges
findings.description: Pricing on a billing document separates the item net price, an optional gross price and price discount, a base quantity, and separately itemised allowances and charges at both line and document level, each with a reason and a reason code. Allowances and charges carry their own tax category, so they are not simple arithmetic adjustments.

questions.text: On what basis is the item price expressed, including base quantity and any gross price and discount?
answer_data: Base quantity and its unit code
Gross price and price discount where present
Currency in which the price is expressed

questions.text: What reason and reason code justifies each allowance or charge, and from which code list is the code drawn?
answer_data: Level at which it applies (line or document)

questions.text: Which tax category and rate apply to each allowance or charge, and how does that interact with the document tax breakdown?
answer_data: Tax category code and rate for the allowance or charge
Contribution to each tax breakdown group
Handling where the category differs from the related line

questions.text: Where an allowance or charge is expressed as a percentage, what base amount is it applied to and is the resulting amount stated explicitly?
answer_data: Resulting amount stated on the document
Consistency check outcome between percentage, base and amount

data_elements.name: Item net price
data_elements.description: Price of the item after any price discount, exclusive of tax.

data_elements.name: Price base quantity
data_elements.description: Quantity to which the item price applies, with its unit code.

data_elements.name: Allowance or charge entry
data_elements.description: An allowance or charge with indicator, amount, optional base and percentage, reason, reason code and tax category.

data_elements.name: Allowance or charge reason code
data_elements.description: Governed code stating why the allowance or charge applies.

artifacts.name: Pricing and adjustment schedule
artifacts.description: Consolidated schedule of prices, base quantities and all line- and document-level allowances and charges with reasons, codes, bases and tax categories, sufficient to reproduce every total independently.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by document authoritative identifier; entries keyed by level, line identifier where applicable, and reason code.

bundles.name: Tax, monetary computation and payment instruction
bundles.description: How the document computes and states tax, in which currencies, how totals must reconcile, and what payment instruction it carries.
bundles.rationale: Tax breakdown, totals and payment instructions are named core elements of an electronic invoice and are the parts most tightly constrained by arithmetic business rules; they are also where an agent most easily produces a plausible but invalid document.

layers.name: Tax treatment and breakdown
layers.description: Tax categories, rates, exemptions and special regimes asserted by the document.

findings.name: Tax breakdown, categories and exemption reasons
findings.description: Tax is stated as a breakdown grouped by category code and rate, each group carrying a taxable amount and a tax amount. Zero-rate, exempt, reverse-charge and out-of-scope categories require an explicit reason, ideally a governed exemption reason code, because absence of tax must be justified rather than merely observed.

questions.text: How are amounts grouped into tax breakdown entries, and what defines a distinct group?
Where no tax or a zero rate is applied, what reason and governed reason code justify it?
answer_data: Exemption reason code and code list version

questions.text: Does a reverse-charge or special regime apply, and what marking does the document carry as a result?
answer_data: Required wording carried on the document
Consequence for the tax amount stated
Jurisdiction whose rule triggers the marking

questions.text: Is a tax representative involved, and how does that change the tax identifiers stated on the document?

data_elements.name: Tax category code
data_elements.description: Governed code stating the tax category applied to an amount group.

data_elements.name: Tax rate
data_elements.description: Percentage rate applied within a tax breakdown group.

data_elements.name: Taxable amount per group
data_elements.description: Sum of amounts subject to the group's category and rate.

data_elements.name: Tax amount per group
data_elements.description: Tax calculated for the group.

data_elements.name: Tax exemption reason code
data_elements.description: Governed code justifying a zero, exempt or out-of-scope category, with code list version.

artifacts.name: Tax breakdown statement
artifacts.description: The complete set of tax breakdown groups with categories, rates, taxable and tax amounts, exemption reasons and codes, sufficient for an authority to reconstruct the tax position of the document.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by document authoritative identifier; groups keyed by category code plus rate.

layers.name: Currency, totals and arithmetic integrity
layers.description: Which currencies the document uses and how its stated totals must reconcile with its parts.

findings.name: Document currency, tax accounting currency and conversion
findings.description: A billing document states amounts in a single document currency, but some jurisdictions require the tax amount also to be stated in a national accounting currency. That produces two tax amounts for the same supply, with a conversion basis that must be declared rather than inferred.

questions.text: In which currency are the document amounts expressed, and from which code list is the currency code drawn?
answer_data: Scope of amounts governed by that currency
Rule forbidding mixed currencies in the same amount set

questions.text: Is a separate tax accounting currency required, and what tax amount is stated in it?
answer_data: Tax total amount in that currency
Jurisdictional rule requiring the second statement
Relationship rule between the two tax amounts

questions.text: What exchange rate, rate source and rate date underpin any conversion, and is that basis stated or merely assumed?
answer_data: Statement of whether the basis is carried on the document or held externally

questions.text: How many decimal places apply to amounts in each currency and how are half-values rounded?
answer_data: Handling of currencies with non-standard minor units

data_elements.name: Document currency code
data_elements.description: Currency in which all document amounts are expressed.

data_elements.name: Tax accounting currency code
data_elements.description: National currency in which the tax amount must additionally be stated where required.

data_elements.name: Tax total in accounting currency
data_elements.description: Tax total expressed in the tax accounting currency.

data_elements.name: Exchange rate basis
data_elements.description: Rate value, publishing source and reference date used for any currency conversion.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Currency selection and conversion basis are scalar assertions carried inside the document and the tax breakdown statement; they produce no independent artefact of their own. The rate source is a reference to an externally governed rate publication owned by a monetary authority, not an artefact this model creates or stores. Where a jurisdiction requires evidence of the rate used, that evidence is captured as a supporting attachment under the attachments finding rather than duplicated here.

findings.name: Document totals, rounding and arithmetic consistency
findings.description: Document totals are not free-form: the sum of line net amounts, document allowances and charges, tax exclusive and inclusive totals, prepaid amount, rounding amount and amount due form a constrained arithmetic system. All fixed and calculated values must be present in the instance because a receiver may not presume an omitted value.

questions.text: Which total amounts must be stated explicitly rather than left for the receiver to compute?
answer_data: Tax exclusive and tax inclusive totals
Prepaid amount, rounding amount and amount due

questions.text: How is each stated total reconciled against its constituent parts, and what tolerance is permitted?
answer_data: Rule identifiers that fire on mismatch
Outcome and evidence of the last reconciliation run

questions.text: When a rounding amount is stated, what does it represent and how is it constrained?
answer_data: Purpose of the rounding (payment convenience, cash rounding)

questions.text: How does a prepaid amount interact with the amount due, and where does the evidence for the prepayment live?
answer_data: Reference to the prepayment evidence or prior document
Statement that settlement state is held in the payment model

data_elements.name: Sum of line net amounts
data_elements.description: Aggregate of all invoice line net amounts.

data_elements.name: Total without tax
data_elements.description: Document total before tax, after document allowances and charges.

data_elements.name: Total with tax
data_elements.description: Document total including tax.

data_elements.name: Prepaid amount
data_elements.description: Amount already paid and deducted from the amount due.

data_elements.name: Rounding amount
data_elements.description: Adjustment applied to reach a rounded amount due.

data_elements.name: Amount due for payment

artifacts.description: Machine-checkable report recording each total, its recomputed value from constituent parts, the rule identifiers applied, the tolerance used and the pass or fail outcome with the instant of execution.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by document authoritative identifier plus rule set version plus execution sequence number.

layers.name: Payment instruction
layers.description: The instruction the document carries for how, when and to whom payment should be made — distinct from settlement itself.

findings.name: Payment means, terms, due date and remittance reference
findings.description: The document carries a payment instruction: a means code, account or mandate details, textual terms, a due date and a remittance or payment reference the payer should quote. This is an assertion at issue time. Whether payment occurred, when, and in what amount is governed by the settlement model and must never be written back into the issued document.

questions.text: By what means is payment requested, and what account, card or mandate details support that means?
answer_data: Payment means code and code list version
Payee account identifier and account name
Card or direct debit mandate details where applicable
Payee party reference where it differs from the seller

questions.text: When is payment due, and how is the due date derived from the terms when only terms are stated?
answer_data: Derivation rule from terms to date
Requirement that one of due date or terms is present

questions.text: What remittance or payment reference must the payer quote, and how does it enable reconciliation?
answer_data: Consequence of the reference being omitted or altered

questions.text: Where is settlement state recorded, and what prevents it being stored as a mutable field on the issued document?
answer_data: Reference to the settlement record set
Rule forbidding mutation of issued document fields
Derivation path for the current outstanding amount
Actor authorised to assert settlement state

data_elements.description: Governed code indicating how payment is to be made.

data_elements.name: Payee account identifier
data_elements.description: Account to which payment should be directed, with the account scheme and account name.

data_elements.name: Payment terms
data_elements.description: Textual statement of payment conditions including any discount or penalty terms.

data_elements.name: Payment due date

data_elements.name: Remittance reference

bundles.name: References, corrections and attachments
bundles.description: What the document points to — orders, contracts, fulfilment records, preceding invoices — and what it carries with it as supporting evidence or human-readable rendition.
bundles.rationale: Contract reference, delivery details and supporting document references are named core elements, and the correction chain is the only lawful way to change an issued invoice; both must be modelled as first-class relationships rather than free text.

layers.name: Commercial and correction references
layers.description: Typed links from the billing document to the commercial documents that justify it and to the documents it corrects or is corrected by.

findings.name: Order, contract and fulfilment references for matching
findings.description: A billing document carries references to the purchase order, sales order, contract, tender or lot, project, despatch advice and receiving advice. These enable two-way and three-way matching and are the practical basis on which a buyer decides to accept or reject.

answer_data: Tolerance rules applied to quantity and price
Matching outcome with the instant of execution

questions.text: How is a dangling or unresolvable reference detected and handled?
answer_data: Handling policy (reject, accept with flag, request clarification)

findings.name: Preceding document reference and the correction chain
findings.description: An issued invoice is not edited. It is amended by a further document that refers specifically and unambiguously to the original — a credit note, a debit note, a corrective invoice or a cancellation, depending on jurisdiction and type. The chain of such documents, not a version history, is the true history of the commercial claim.

questions.text: Which preceding document does this document amend, and how specifically and unambiguously is it identified?
answer_data: Preceding document identifier and its issue date
Identifier scheme used for the reference
Referenced line identifiers where the correction is partial
Assessment that the reference is unambiguous

answer_data: Mechanism used (credit note, debit note, corrective invoice, cancellation)
Effect on the original document's validity

questions.text: What guarantees that the corrected original remains retrievable and unmodified after correction?
answer_data: Immutability control applied to the original
Digest of the original recorded before correction
Retrieval path for the superseded document

questions.text: How is the net commercial effect of a correction chain computed across all linked documents?
answer_data: Ordered chain of linked document identifiers

artifacts.description: Directed graph of billing documents linked by supersession, credit and debit relations, with signed amount contributions and the digest of each superseded document, enabling the net claim to be recomputed and audited.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Nodes keyed by each document's authoritative identifier; edges keyed by source identifier, target identifier and relation type.

layers.name: Attachments and human-readable renditions
layers.description: Supporting documents carried with or referenced by the invoice, and the human-readable form of the invoice itself.

findings.name: Supporting attachments and the human-readable rendition
findings.description: An invoice may carry supporting documents as embedded binary objects or external references, each with a media type and filename. Separately, the invoice itself often has a human-readable rendition; in hybrid formats a single PDF/A-3 file embeds the structured XML, so one file carries two representations of the same invoice and their precedence must be declared. Legibility must be maintained for the whole storage period.

answer_data: Font, resource and colour-space embedding evidence
Periodic legibility check outcomes with instants
Migration policy if the format becomes unreadable

answer_data: Binding of digests into the signed or sealed scope
Handling of attachments outside the signature scope

bundles.name: Lifecycle, authenticity and regulatory conformance
bundles.description: How the document moves through states, how the receiver responds, what makes it trustworthy, and how its legal conformance is established and evidenced.
bundles.rationale: Authenticity of origin, integrity of content and legibility are explicit legal requirements from issue to the end of the storage period, satisfiable by business controls creating a reliable audit trail as well as by signatures or EDI; clearance regimes add a further authority-side step that changes the lifecycle.

layers.name: Lifecycle states and receiver response
layers.description: The states a billing document occupies and the responses a receiver may make.

findings.name: Lifecycle states, transitions and immutability point
findings.description: A billing document passes through preparation, issue, transmission, delivery, receipt, acceptance or rejection, correction and archiving. The decisive property is that content becomes immutable at issue: subsequent change is achieved by a new document, not by editing. Under clearance regimes an authority step is inserted before the document may lawfully be delivered.

questions.text: What is the permitted state set for this document type and which transitions are legal between them?

answer_data: Immutability trigger event and its instant
Fields that may still change and why

answer_data: Inserted state and its entry and exit conditions
Status of a document delivered without clearance

questions.text: How is each transition recorded so that the state history can be reconstructed independently of current state?

findings.name: Buyer response, rejection and dispute
findings.description: Business acceptance is a separate act from transport delivery. A receiver may acknowledge, accept, conditionally accept, reject or dispute a billing document, with reasons that should be coded so the issuer can act automatically. Dispute suspends the practical expectation of payment without altering the document.

answer_data: Silence semantics where no response is returned

questions.text: How is a rejection or dispute reason coded so that the issuer can act on it without human reading?
answer_data: Reason code and code list version

questions.text: Who within the receiving organisation is authorised to accept, reject or dispute, and how is that authority evidenced?
answer_data: Monetary or category limits on the authority
Escalation path when the limit is exceeded

questions.text: What effect does a dispute have on the payment due date and on retention obligations?
answer_data: Dispute state and its start instant
Effect on the asserted due date

data_elements.description: The business response returned by the receiver.

data_elements.name: Response reason code
data_elements.description: Coded reason for rejection, conditional acceptance or dispute.

data_elements.name: Dispute state

artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by its own message identifier from the responding system, linked to the referenced document's authoritative identifier.

findings.name: Self-billing, prepayment and special processes
findings.description: UN/CEFACT CII treats traditional supplier-initiated invoices and self-billing as first-class processes; the customer raises a self-billing invoice and the supplier reconciles it, raising a dispute notice on discrepancy, corrected by a self-billing credit note. UBL SelfBilledInvoice is created by the Customer Accounting Party. Article 226(10a) requires the mention 'Self-billing'. Prepayment invoices (386) collect amounts to be subtracted from a final invoice. CII also names consolidated, consignment and factored variants. These are rare relative to 380 but are not optional footnotes in a full model.

questions.text: Is this a self-billed invoice, which agreement authorises it, and has the supplier accepted or disputed it?

Is the invoice consolidated, consignment (non-sale), factored or freight-charge billing, and which process rules then apply?

layers.name: Authenticity, integrity and authority clearance
layers.description: The controls and authority acts that make the document trustworthy as evidence.

findings.name: Authenticity of origin, integrity of content and business controls
findings.description: Authenticity of origin and integrity of content must be assured from issue to the end of the storage period. The law is technology-neutral: any business controls creating a reliable audit trail between the invoice and the supply are acceptable, with advanced electronic signature and EDI named as examples rather than as mandatory methods. A model that assumes signatures are required overstates the requirement.

answer_data: Assurance method (business controls, electronic signature or seal, EDI)

Description of the control that creates the link

Actor responsible for maintaining the trail

questions.text: Where a signature or seal is applied, what exact byte scope does it cover and what does it leave unprotected?
answer_data: Elements or attachments outside the scope
Verification outcome with instant and verifying actor

questions.text: How is assurance maintained for the whole storage period as algorithms and certificates age?
answer_data: Long-term validation or archival timestamp strategy
Re-protection schedule and last execution instant

findings.name: Tax authority clearance, registration and reporting acknowledgement
findings.description: In continuous transaction control regimes the tax authority or its agent registers the invoice before or at the moment of issue and returns an identifier, an acknowledgement instant and often a signed code. That authority-side identifier is the master-system identifier for that jurisdiction and outranks the issuer's own number for legal purposes.

answer_data: Deadline duration and its measurement basis

layers.name: Regulatory conformance and validation evidence
layers.description: Which particulars the law requires, how jurisdictional variants change them, and what evidence proves the document was checked.

findings.name: Mandatory particulars and jurisdictional variants
findings.description: The governing law prescribes an exhaustive list of particulars a full invoice must show, with reduced sets for simplified invoices and additional wording for special regimes. National usage specifications further constrain or extend the core semantic model, and language and translation obligations may apply during storage. Conformance is therefore always jurisdiction-qualified.

answer_data: Governing jurisdiction and its determination basis

questions.text: Which national or sectoral usage specification applies on top of the core model, and what does it change?
answer_data: Restrictions and additions relative to the core

answer_data: Party responsible for producing a translation

bundles.name: Exchange, retention and governance
bundles.description: How the document is serialised and routed, how long it must be kept and how it is disposed of, and who owns, may access and must be able to audit it.
bundles.rationale: Syntax binding, network routing, storage obligations and role-scoped access are the operating surface an agent must handle to move an invoice between organisations lawfully; storage obligations and the acceptability of storage location are set by law, while transport is set by network specifications.

layers.name: Serialisation, routing and delivery evidence
layers.description: How the same invoice semantics are carried across syntaxes and networks without loss, and what evidence exists that it arrived.

findings.name: Syntax binding and semantic fidelity across serialisations
findings.description: The same invoice semantics are bound to different syntaxes — a business-language XML document family, a cross-industry XML syntax, and hybrid carriers embedding one inside a rendition. Bindings are not bijective: extensions, code-list versions and structural differences make round-tripping lossy, so fidelity must be measured rather than assumed.

layers.name: Retention, storage and disposition
layers.description: How long the document and its evidence must be kept, where, in what condition, and how it is lawfully destroyed.

findings.name: Retention period, storage conditions, holds and erasure conflict
findings.description: Both issuer and recipient must retain invoices for a period fixed by national law, keeping authenticity, integrity and legibility intact and making them accessible to authorities on request; storage location and method are otherwise flexible. Retention interacts badly with personal-data erasure rights, and a legal hold must be able to suspend disposition without altering the record.

findings.name: Ownership, custodianship and role-scoped projections
findings.description: The issuing party owns the record; a service provider, access point or archiving provider may hold and process it as custodian without acquiring ownership. Different roles need different slices — a routing party needs envelope metadata only, an auditor needs the evidentiary set, a tax authority needs the full particulars — so projections are the access mechanism, not ad hoc field hiding.

findings.description: Every act on the document — generation, transformation, signing, clearance, transmission, validation, storage, disclosure, disposition — is recorded with the acting party, the acting system and an instant, distinguishing when the act happened from when it was observed. This is what allows an agent to answer for the document years later.
